NEWS 2026-11-19 Moneycontrol (GTA VI launch: Why gamers around the world turned into honorary New Zealanders):
Players across the globe this week became “honorary New Zealanders” in an effort to get the most-anticipated video game of all time just a few hours early.
Grand Theft Auto VI rolled out at midnight in each time zone on Nov. 19, making the island nation one of the first markets to gain access. Countless eager gamers said they changed the region of their console in order to secure early access, triggering active online discussions about other ways to game the system.
Even the government of New Zealand got in on the fun with a welcoming post on Instagram.
The gradual global rollout is a common practice with major new video games and the loophole of marking oneself a New Zealand resident is a long-established practice that console makers are well aware of. Microsoft Corp.’s regional Xbox account acknowledged it back in 2021 with the launch of Forza Horizon 5, and Thursday morning saw people flocking to social media and streaming platforms to share the tip.
“We heard a few of you are trying the New Zealand trick to join us,” New Zealand’s official tourism agency said in an Instagram reel filled with bucolic scenes from around the country. Responding to a person who said they’d done it several times, the agency added, “Surely there’s a rule that you need to visit once every three times you’ve faked it.”
GTA6 is now the best-reviewed game of all time and its release is widely expected to set new highs for revenue and popularity. The $80 Rockstar Games title has notched $1.65 billion in sales already, with three quarters of that on Sony Group Corp.’s PlayStation platform and the rest on Microsoft’s Xbox Series X and S, according to industry research house SensorTower, which has set up a dedicated page to track the historic game.
“The launch of Grand Theft Auto VI may have done what no central bank could: get traders to step away from their screens,” said Eric Xiao, head of Asia sales at CMC Markets. “Overall trading activity on our platform fell 53.82% last night versus the previous Thursday. Plenty of clients, it seems, swapped charts for controllers.”
Many of those who kept working traded the theme. Volume in Take-Two Interactive Software Inc., the game’s publisher, jumped 206% week on week and its shares rose 6.2% on Wednesday. Benchmark trading volumes on mega-cap AI stocks such as Microsoft and Nvidia Corp. decreased by an average of about 57%.
Beside its appeal as a video game experience, GTA6 is also set to accelerate trends in online entertainment. SOURCE newsweek.com (PlayStation Issues GTA 6 Software Warning Before Launch):
Owners of PlayStation 5 consoles have been told they must update their software before they can play Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) when it launches on Thursday.
“Sony Interactive has issued a PS5 system software update that is required before playing Grand Theft Auto VI,” PlayStation Support US wrote on X. “Players should download this update prior to midnight on November 19 so that they’re ready to play on launch day, November 19.”
GTA 6 is arriving more than a decade after the release of Grand Theft Auto V, making Thursday’s launch a major event for players who have waited years for Rockstar Games' next installment.
Read More on News
Rockstar has advised players to prepare their consoles ahead of the release, given it requires up to 212 GB of space.
The game becomes playable at midnight local time on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S consoles.
Newsweek has contacted Rockstar Games for comment via email. Newsweek also reached out to Sony Interactive Entertainment via online contact form.
More Than 15 Million Pre-Orders—Estimate
Even before its launch, the game has made more than $1.5 billion in sales, according to an unofficial estimate.
A tracker from Sensor Tower, a market research firm, says the game had an estimated 15.88 million digital pre-orders across PS5 and Xbox Series X|S as of Tuesday. Those sales were worth approximately $1.54 billion, according to the tracker.
Rockstar Games has not confirmed how many pre-orders have been placed.
Grand Theft Auto V is one of the bestselling video games ever made and reached $1 billion in retail sales in just three days.
Altogether, the GTA franchise has sold more than 470 million units worldwide, with Grand Theft Auto V accounting for more than 230 million of those sales.
Players Told to Check Their Consoles
Rockstar Games says the GTA 6 pre-load requires up to 212GB of available space, depending on the device.
Players have been advised they may need to free storage on their consoles, configure automatic downloads and allow enough time for the installation to finish.
Players short on internal space can also expand their console storage; PS5 supports compatible M.2 NVMe SSDs, while Xbox Series X|S supports dedicated Storage Expansion Cards capable of running current-generation games directly.
Automatic downloading also depends on the console's settings. PS5 owners need auto-downloads enabled and the machine either switched on or in Rest Mode. Xbox players need automatic updates enabled and their console switched on or in Sleep mode.
What Players Should Do Before Launch
PlayStation recommends checking that a pre-order was successful, enabling auto-download, keeping the PS5 connected to the internet in Rest Mode and making sure its system software is up to date. Players can check remaining capacity under Settings > Storage and confirm whether the pre-load has started through their Game Library.
Xbox Series X|S players should also make sure they have enough free storage and that automatic updates are enabled. Rockstar says an Xbox must be switched on or placed in Sleep mode for automatic pre-loading to work.
If a pre-load stalls or returns an error, players should first check their console’s internet connection and available storage, then restart the download if necessary. Rockstar also directs PS5 and Xbox Series X|S users experiencing pre-load problems to the relevant PlayStation or Xbox troubleshooting guidance.
Contact Newsweek editors on this story: Rebecca Flood and Cristina Diciu.

SOURCE androidauthority.com (Sony issues mandatory PS5 update for playing GTA 6 at launch):
Sony says this PS5 update is mandatory if you want to play GTA 6 at launch
Nov 17, 2026 — 10:50 PM ET
- Sony has released a mandatory PS5 system software update that players need to install before playing GTA 6.
- The update is around 1GB in size and includes security fixes, although Sony hasn’t detailed any GTA 6-specific changes.
- Sony is urging players to install the update before November 19 so they’re ready to play on launch day.
Sony has one final request for PlayStation 5 owners ahead of the much-anticipated launch of Grand Theft Auto VI, i.e., update your console before launching the game.
The company has confirmed that the latest PS5 system software update is mandatory for playing GTA 6, asking players to download and install it before midnight on November 19 so they can jump into the game as soon as it launches.
Sony Interactive has issued a PS5 system software update that is required before playing Grand Theft Auto VI. Players should download this update prior to midnight on November 19 so that they’re ready to play on launch day, November 19.
The announcement came through the official PlayStation Support US account on X, with Sony warning players not to leave the system update until the last minute. GTA 6 is scheduled to launch at midnight on November 19, 2026, with availability following local time zones.
The update carries version number 26.07-14.23.00 and began rolling out on November 17. While the download is relatively small, it is larger than a typical minor patch, weighing in at around 1.3GB.
Sony’s official changelog doesn’t mention any GTA 6-specific improvements. It lists just one change: “We’ve made some security fixes to the system software.” The previous PS5 firmware update, version 26.07-14.22.00, also focused on security fixes.
Sony hasn’t explained why GTA 6 specifically requires this firmware version. However, the timing is notable, with the company releasing back-to-back security updates as the PS5 faces increased scrutiny over jailbreaks and software exploits.
Players who haven’t installed the update can manually check for it by heading to Settings > System > System Software > System Software Update and Settings on their PS5.
